  "output": "# Bots in Campfire

Campfire supports chat bots that can be members of rooms and post messages via an HTTP API.

## Architecture

- **`Bot` Model**: Stored in the `bots` table, belonging to a creator (`User`) and associated with a backing `User` record that represents the bot within the chat system.
  - Generates a secure, unique `code` credential (`has_secure_token :code`) used for authenticating message posts.
  - Manages its bot name and avatar, keeping the underlying `User` name and ActiveStorage avatar in sync.
  - Automatically joins all open rooms on creation (`after_create_commit :grant_membership_to_open_rooms` via the backing user).
  - Can be added to closed rooms just like human users via room member selection.
  - On deletion, deactivates its backing user (removing room memberships) and deletes the `Bot` record, revoking API posting access.

- **Account Settings Integration**:
  - Accessible to all members from Account Settings (`/account/edit`) via the bot icon ("Set up chat bots").
  - Bots are excluded from the account users list on `/account/edit` so they are managed exclusively from `/bots`.

- **Bot Management UI (`/bots`)**:
  - Displays all bots created by the current user (administrators see all bots).
  - Renders all bots on a single page without pagination.
  - Each list item displays the bot name, avatar, unique bot code in a read-only field labelled "Bot code", and an "Edit <bot name>" link.
  - "Add a chat bot" button opens `/bots/new`.
  - Edit page (`/bots/:id/edit`) includes the edit form and a "Delete this chat bot" button with native browser confirmation dialog.

## HTTP API

Bots post messages via a simple HTTP POST endpoint:

```bash
curl -d "Deploy of v1.2.3 finished ✅" \
  https://chat.example.com/rooms/<room-id>/<bot-code>/messages
```

The raw request body becomes the message body without any JSON envelope or required field names.

### Responses

- `201 Created`: Message successfully created, with `Location: /messages/:message_id`.
- `422 Unprocessable Content`: Empty message body and no attachment.
- `404 Not Found`: Bad room id, or bot is not a member of the room.
- `401 Unauthorized`: Invalid bot code, or bot has been deleted.

### Notifications and Broadcasting

Messages created by bots are broadcast to connected clients via Turbo Streams and ActionCable and trigger web push notifications to subscribed room members, identical to human-authored messages, displaying the bot's name and avatar as author.

class Room < ApplicationRecord
  has_many :memberships, dependent: :delete_all do
    def grant_to(users)
      room = proxy_association.owner
      Membership.insert_all(Array(users).collect { |user| { room_id: room.id, user_id: user.id, involvement: room.default_involvement } })
    end

    end

    def revise(granted: [], revoked: [])
      transaction do
        grant_to(granted) if granted.present?
        revoke_from(revoked) if revoked.present?
      end
    end
  end

  has_many :users, through: :memberships
  has_many :messages, dependent: :destroy

  belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User", default: -> { Current.user }

  validate :direct_rooms_keep_their_type, on: :update

  scope :opens,           -> { where(type: "Rooms::Open") }
  scope :closeds,         -> { where(type: "Rooms::Closed") }
  scope :directs,         -> { where(type: "Rooms::Direct") }
  scope :without_directs, -> { where.not(type: "Rooms::Direct") }

  scope :ordered, -> { order("LOWER(name)") }

  class << self
    def create_for(attributes, users:)
      transaction do
        create!(attributes).tap do |room|
          room.memberships.grant_to users
        end
      end
    end

    def original
      order(:created_at).first
    end
  end

  def receive(message)
    unread_memberships(message)
    push_later(message)
    trigger_bot_mentions_later(message)
  end

  def open?
    is_a?(Rooms::Open)
  end

  def closed?
    is_a?(Rooms::Closed)
  end

  def direct?
    is_a?(Rooms::Direct)
  end

  def default_involvement
    "mentions"
  end

  private
    # Open and closed rooms convert into each other freely. A direct room can't become
    # either: its participants agreed to a private conversation, not to one whose
    # audience someone else gets to widen afterwards.
    def direct_rooms_keep_their_type
      if type_changed? && type_was == "Rooms::Direct"
        errors.add :type, "can't be changed for a direct room"
      end
    end

    def unread_memberships(message)
      memberships.visible.disconnected.where.not(user: message.creator).update_all(unread_at: message.created_at, updated_at: Time.current)

    def push_later(message)
      Room::PushMessageJob.perform_later(self, message)

      message.mentioned_bots.each do |bot|

require "net/http"

class Bot::WebhookDelivery
  attr_reader :bot, :message
  delegate :room, to: :message

  def initialize(bot:, message:)
    @bot = bot
    @message = message
  end

  def deliver
    return if bot.webhook_url.blank?

    uri = URI.parse(bot.webhook_url)
    return unless uri.is_a?(URI::HTTP) || uri.is_a?(URI::HTTPS)

    request = Net::HTTP::Post.new(uri.request_uri)
    request["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
    request.body = payload.to_json

    response = Net::HTTP.start(uri.host, uri.port, use_ssl: uri.scheme == "https", open_timeout: 5, read_timeout: 15) do |http|
      http.request(request)
    end

    handle_response(response)
  rescue StandardError => e
    Rails.logger.error "Bot #{bot.id} webhook delivery failed: #{e.class} - #{e.message}"
  end

  def payload
    {
      event: "mention",
      author: {
        id: message.creator.id,
        name: message.creator.name
      },
      room: {
        id: room.id,
        name: room.name,
        reply_to: Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.room_bot_messages_path(room, bot.code)
      },
      message: {
        id: message.id,
        body: {
          text: stripped_text,
          html: html_body
        },
        link: Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.room_at_message_path(room, message)
      }
    }
  end

  private
    def stripped_text
      text = if message.body&.body
        message.body.body.render_attachments(with_full_attributes: false) do |attachment|
          attachment.attachable == bot.user ? "" : attachment.to_plain_text
        end.fragment.to_plain_text
      else
        message.plain_text_body
      end

      text = text.gsub(/(?:^|\s)@#{Regexp.escape(bot.name)}[:,]?(?=\s|$)/i, "").strip
      text = text.sub(/\A[:,]\s*/, "").strip
      text
    end

    def html_body
      message.body&.body&.to_html.to_s
    end

    def handle_response(response)
      return unless response.code == "200"

      content_type = response.content_type.to_s.downcase
      return unless %w[text/plain text/html].include?(content_type)

      body = response.body.to_s.force_encoding("UTF-8").strip
      return if body.blank?

      bot_message = room.messages.create_with_attachment!(
        creator: bot.user,
        body: body
      )
      bot_message.broadcast_create
    end
end
EOF

class Bot::WebhookDelivery
  attr_reader :bot, :message
  delegate :room, to: :message

  def initialize(bot:, message:)
    @bot = bot
    @message = message
  end

  def deliver
    return if bot.webhook_url.blank?

    uri = URI.parse(bot.webhook_url)
    return unless uri.is_a?(URI::HTTP) || uri.is_a?(URI::HTTPS)

    request = Net::HTTP::Post.new(uri.request_uri)
    request["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
    request.body = payload.to_json

      http.request(request)
    end

    handle_response(response)
  rescue StandardError => e
    Rails.logger.error "Bot #{bot.id} webhook delivery failed: #{e.class} - #{e.message}"
  end

  def payload
    {
      event: "mention",
      author: {
        id: message.creator.id,
        name: message.creator.name
      },
      room: {
        id: room.id,
        name: room.name,
        reply_to: Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.room_bot_messages_path(room, bot.code)
      },
      message: {
        id: message.id,
        body: {
          text: stripped_text,
          html: html_body
        },
        link: Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.room_at_message_path(room, message)
      }
    }
  end

  private
    def stripped_text
      text = if message.body&.body
        message.body.body.render_attachments(with_full_attributes: false) do |attachment|
          attachment.attachable == bot.user ? "" : attachment.to_plain_text
        end.fragment.to_plain_text
      else
        message.plain_text_body
      end

      text = text.gsub(/(?:^|\s)@#{Regexp.escape(bot.name)}[:,]?(?=\s|$)/i, "").strip
      text = text.sub(/\A[:,]\s*/, "").strip
      text.gsub(/[^\S\r\n]+/, " ").strip
    end

    def html_body
      message.body&.body&.to_html.to_s
    end

    def handle_response(response)
      return unless response.code == "200"

      content_type = response.content_type.to_s.downcase
      return unless %w[text/plain text/html].include?(content_type)

      body = response.body.to_s.dup.force_encoding("UTF-8").strip
      return if body.blank?

steps.message:
I have implemented the bot webhook callback feature according to all specifications:

1. **Database & Model**:
   - Added `webhook_url` column to the `bots` table via an ActiveRecord migration.
   - Normalized `webhook_url` in `Bot` model so empty strings or whitespace values clear the webhook (`nil`).

2. **UI & Forms**:
   - Added the optional "Webhook URL" field to both `/bots/new` and `/bots/:id/edit` via `app/views/bots/_form.html.erb`, with visible label "Webhook URL", placeholder "Webhook URL", and aria-label "Webhook URL".
   - Permitted `webhook_url` parameter in `BotsController`.

3. **Mention Webhook Dispatch**:
   - Extended `Message::Mentionee` with `mentioned_bots` to identify mentioned bots in messages.
   - When a user posts a message mentioning a bot, `Room#receive` asynchronously enqueues `Bot::DeliverWebhookJob` (backed by `Bot::WebhookDelivery`), ensuring message creation is never delayed.
   - Bot creators cannot trigger webhooks on themselves or other bots.

4. **Payload & Bot Responses**:
   - Delivered payload via HTTP POST with `Content-Type: application/json` formatted with `event`, `author`, `room` (including `reply_to`), and `message` (with deep link and stripped text command).
   - Stripped the bot's own mention from `message.body.text` for both ActionText attachments and plain text commands.
   - Handled synchronous responses: `200` with `text/plain` or `text/html` creates a message in the room authored by the bot and broadcasts it via Turbo Streams; `204` posts no message.
   - Supported asynchronous replies via `POST <reply_to>` with raw text or JSON.

5. **Documentation & Tests**:
   - Updated `docs/bots.md` with webhook architecture, payload format, and reply methods.
   - Added comprehensive tests across models and controllers covering webhook form inputs, payload generation, mention stripping, synchronous bot responses, and error handling.

I will now submit the final output.
